expilo.definition: ex-pīlō āvī, ātus, āre, to pillage, rob, plnnder: aerarium, S.: ad expilandos socios: fanum Apollinis: genis oculos, pluck, O.—Fig.; ii, a quibus expilati sumus.

expingo.definition: ex-pingō —, pictus, ere, to depict, describe to the life: motus hominum expictus.

expio.definition: ex-piō āvī, ātus, āre.—In religion, to make amends for, atone for, purify, expiate, purge by sacrifice: tua scelera in nostros milites, i. e. avenge: filium pecuniā publicā, L.: quae violata sunt, expiabuntur: arma No…

expiscor.definition: ex-piscor ātus, ārī, dep., to fish out, search out, find out: proinde expiscare, quasi non nosses, T.: nihil, to inquire no further.

explanatio.definition: explānātiō ōnis, f explano, an explanation, interpretation : religionis. — Plur: interpretum: portentorum.— As a rhet. figure, C.

explanator.definition: explānātor ōris, m explano, an interpreter .

explano.definition: explānō āvī, ātus, āre ex + planus, to make plain, make clear, explain : qualis differentia sit, etc.: rem definiendo: de hominis moribus pauca, S.: carmen, L.

expleo.definition: expleō ēvī (explēris, C., V.; explē ssent, L.; explēsse, V.), ētus, ēre PLE-, to fill up, fill full, fill, stuff : fossam aggere, Cs.: rimas: bovem frondibus, H.: locum (cohortes), Cs.—Of number or quantity, to fill, …

expletio.definition: explētiō ōnis, f expleo, a satisfying : naturae.

explicatio.definition: explicātiō ōnis, f explico, an unfolding, uncoiling : rudentis. — Fig., an unfolding, expounding, exposition, explanation : rerum facilis: fabularum.

explicator.definition: explicātor ōris, m explico, an expounder, explainer : rerum.

explicatrix.definition: explicātrīx īcis, f explicator, she that explains : vis dicendi, explicatrix orationis.

explico.definition: ex-plicō āvī and uī, ātus or itus, ā re, to unfold, uncoil, unroll, unfurl, unclose, spread out, loosen, undo: explicatā veste: volumen: frondes, V.: frontem sollicitam, smooth, H.: seria contractae frontis, H. — Refl…

explodo.definition: explōdō sī, sus, ere ex + plaudo, to drive out, hiss away, hoot off : Aesopum explodi video: explosa Arbuscula, H. — To reject, disapprove : quod tum explosum est: sententias.

exploratio.definition: explōrātiō ōnis, f exploro, an examination : occulta, Ta.

explorator.definition: explōrātor ōris, m exploro, an explorer, spy, scout : per exploratores certior factus, Cs.: iter hostium ab exploratoribus edoctus, Ta.

exploro.definition: ex-plōrō āvī, ātus, āre, to cause to flow forth, bring out, search out, examine, investigate, explore: rem totam: fugam domini: caecum iter, O.: locos novos, V.: idoneum locum castris, select, Cs.: de voluntate alcius…

expolio.definition: expoliō īvī, ītus, īre, to smooth, polish, finish, adorn, embellish, refine, elaborate: nox te expolivit: Dionem doctrinis omnibus.

expolitio.definition: expolītiō ōnis, f expolio, a smoothing off, polishing, finishing, embellishing : urbana, i. e. of a house in the city.— Plur. : utriusque nostrūm, i. e. of both our houses .—Fig.: inest in numero expolitio.

expono.definition: ex-pōnō posuī, positus (expostus, V.), ere, to put out, set forth, expose, exhibit: vasa: argentum in aedibus: ratis Expositis stabat scalis, laid out, V.: alqd venditioni, Ta.—Of children, to expose, abandon: Is quic…

exporrigo.definition: ex-porrigō —, —, ere, to spread out.—Only imper: exporge frontem (i. e. exporrige), smooth, T.

exportatio.definition: exportātiō ōnis, f exporto, a carrying out, exportation : rerum: his exportationibus HS LX perdidisse.

exporto.definition: ex-portō āvī, ātus, āre, to carry out, bring out, convey away, send away, export: aurum ex Italiā Hierosolymam: frumentum in fame: vim mellis Syracusis: corpora tectis, V.: sua omnia, Cs.

exposco.definition: ex-pōscō popōscī, —, ere, to ask earnestly, beg, request, entreat, implore: quam (misericordiam): signum proeli, Cs.: pacem precibus, L.: pacem Teucris (dat.), V.: alqd deos, L.: Aenean acciri, V.: audire labores, V.:…

expositio.definition: expositiō ōnis, f expositus, a setting forth, exposition, narration, citation, explanation : rerum: sententiae suae: summi boni.

expostulatio.definition: expostulātiō ōnis, f expostulo, a pressing demand : bonorum: singulorum, Ta.— An expostulation, complaint : tua: cum esset expostulatio facta.—Plur: cum absente Pompeio: suae, L.

expostulo.definition: ex-postulō āvī, ātus, āre, to demand pressingly, insist on: alqd, Ta.: ut Hiberi decedant, Ta.: Armeniam vacuam fieri, Ta. — To find fault, dispute, expostulate, complain of: iracundius: cum eo iniuriam hanc, T.: nihi…

exprimo.definition: exprimō pressī, pressus, ere ex + premo, to press out, force out, squeeze forth : (lacrimulam) oculos terendo, T.: nubium conflictu ardor expressus: has (turrīs) cottidianus agger expresserat, had carried up , Cs.: ex…

exprobratio.definition: exprobrātiō ōnis, f exprobro, a reproaching, upbraiding : benefici, T.: cuiquam fortunae, L.

exprobro.definition: exprobrō āvī, ātus, āre ex+probrum, to reproach with, blame for, find fault, charge, upbraid, reproach : exprobrandi causā dicere: suam quisque militiam, L.: beneficia apud memores, L.: casūs bellicos tibi, throw the …

expromo.definition: ex-prōmō prōmpsī, prōmptus, ere, to show forth, discover, exert, practise, exhibit, display: supplicia in civīs: apparatūs supplicii, L.: vigilandi laborem in cenis.—To give utterance to, utter, disclose, express, sta…

expugnabilis.definition: expūgnābilis e, adj. expugno, that may be taken by assault, assailable : urbs, L.: arx magnis exercitibus, Ta.

expugnatio.definition: expūgnātiō ōnis, f expugno, a taking by assault, storming : urbis, Cs.: hostilis. — Plur: aedificiorum.

expugnator.definition: expūgnātor ōris, m expugno, a stormer, capturer : urbis.—Fig.: pudicitiae.

expugnax.definition: (expūgnāx, ācis) adj. expugno, victorious, effectual .—Only comp: expugnacior herba, O.

expugno.definition: ex-pūgnō āvī, ātus, āre, to take by assault, storm, capture, reduce, subdue: urbīs per vim, Cs.: Cirtam armis, S.: quam (turrim), V.: iuvenum domos, H.: ipsum caput, i. e. the old man in person, H.—To subdue, overcome…

expulsio.definition: expulsiō ōnis, f 1 PAL-, a driving out, expulsion : Laenatis.—Plur: civium.

expulsor.definition: expulsor ōris, m 1 PAL-, a driver out, expeller : bonorum: tyranni, N.

expultrix.definition: expultrīx īcis, f expulsor, she that expels : philosophia vitiorum.

expurgo.definition: ex-pūrgō āvī, ātus, āre, to purge, cleanse, purify: me, i. e. cure of poetic ecstasy, H. — Fig.: expurgandus est sermo.—To clear from censure, exculpate, vindicate, justify, excuse: me, T.: sese parum, fail to vindica…

exquiro.definition: exquīrō sīvī, sītus, ere ex+quaero, to search out, seek diligently, inquire into, scrutinize, inquire, ask : ex te causas divinationis: haec nimis a Graecis, to be too exacting in : Ancillas cruciatu, T.: secum, quid …

exsacrifico.definition: ex-sacrificō (-cruficō) —, —, āre, to sacrifice: hostiis balantibus, Enn. ap. C.

exsaevio.definition: ex-saeviō —, —, īre, to cease raging: dum reliquum tempestatis exsaeviret, L.

exsanguis.definition: ex-sanguis (exang-) e (no gen. or dat; in plur. only nom.), adj., without blood, bloodless, lifeless: corpora mortuorum: umbrae, V.—Pale, wan, exhausted, feeble: genae: exsanguis et mortuus concidisti: metu, O.: visu,…

exsarcio.definition: ex-sarciō or exerciō —, rtūrus, īre, to patch, mend, repair: sumptum suom, repay their cost, T.

exsatio.definition: ex-satiō āvī, ātus, āre, to satisfy, glut, sate: exsatiati cibo, L.: clade exsatiata domus, O.: patruum sanguine domūs, Ta.

exsaturabilis.definition: exsaturābilis e, adj. exsaturo, that may be sated : nec exsaturabile pectus, insatiate , V.

exsaturo.definition: ex-saturō (exat-) —, ātus, āre, to satisfy satiate, sate: belua exsaturanda visceribus meis, O.: exsaturata lubido, Poët. ap. C.: eius supplicio animum: odiis exsaturata quievi, V.

exscindo.definition: ex-scindō or excindō idī, issus, ere, to extirpate, annihilate, destroy: templum sanctitatis: quae urbs se exscindi pateretur: finī s tuos, L.: ferro gentem, V.: virtutem, Ta.

exscribo.definition: ex-scrībō (excr-) īpsī, īptus, ere, to write out, write off, copy: tabulas: exscribendi potestas.

exsculpo.definition: ex-sculpō or exculpō psī, ptus, ere, to dig out, cut out, chisel out, carve: nescio quid e quercu. —To scratch out, erase: versūs, N.—Fig., to elicit, extort: ex aliquo verum, T.

exseco.definition: ex-secō or execō cuī, ctus, āre, to cut out, cut away, remove: vitiosas partīs: linguam: cornu exsecto frons, H.: nervis urbis exsectis: Lichan iam matre peremptā, V.—To cut, castrate: alqm. —To deduct, take out, exto…

exsecrabilis.definition: exsecrābilis (execr-) e, adj. exsecror, accursed : fortuna, L.— Cursing, execrating : carmen, L.: odium in bis captos, i. e. bitter , L.

exsecratio.definition: exsecrātiō (execr-) ōnis, f exsecror, an execration, malediction, curse : Thyestea.— An oath with imprecation : hunc exsecratione devinxerat: post execrationem degustare, S.

exsecror.definition: exsecror or execror ātus, ārī, dep. ex + sacro, to curse, utter curses, execrate, abhor : te: Catilinae consilia, S.: terram Ulixi, V.: in se, L.: haec in se: ut pereat Atreus: verba exsecrantia, O.— To take an oath w…

exsectio.definition: exsectiō (exect-) ōnis, f 2 SAC-, a cutting out, excision : linguae: fundi.

exsecutio.definition: exsecūtiō ōnis, f exsequor, an accomplishing : negotii, Ta.: Syriae, i. e. absolute power in , Ta.

exsequiae.definition: exsequiae or exequiae ārum, f SEC-, a funeral procession, funeral obsequies : convenire ad exsequias cohonestandas: Ante urbem exsequiae Significant luctum, O.: fertur in exsequiis matrona, O.: exsequiis rite solutis,…

exsequialis.definition: exsequiālis (exequ-) e, adj. exsequiae, of a funeral, funereal : carmina, dirges , O.

exsequor.definition: ex-sequor or exequor cūtus, ī, dep., to follow to the grave: Hunc omni laude, C. poët.— Fig., to follow, follow after, accompany, go after, pursue: cladem illam fugamque: fatum illius, i. e. share: suam quisque spem, …

exsero.definition: ex-serō ruī, rtus, ere, to stretch out, thrust out, put forth, take out: manum ad mentum, L.: bracchia aquis, O.: via quā se exsereret, come forth, O. —Fig.: se aere alieno.—P. perf., thrust out, protruding, bare, unc…

exserto.definition: exsertō —, —, āre, freq. exsero, to stretch out, thrust forth : Ora, V.

exsibilo.definition: ex-sībilō —, —, āre, to hiss out, hiss from the stage: histrio exsibilatur.

exsicco.definition: ex-siccō āvī, ātus, āre, to dry up, make dry: arbores.—To drink up: vina culullis, H.

exsigno.definition: ex-sīgnō —, ātus, āre, to write out, note down: sacra omnia exsignata, L.

exsilio.definition: exsiliō or exiliō iluī, —, īre ex + salio, to spring out, spring forth, leap up, start up, bound : ad te, T.: de sellā: domo levis exsilit, H.: protinus, O.: (anguis) in siccum, V.: gaudio: exsiluere oculi, started ou…

exsilium.definition: exsilium or exilium ī, n exsul, banishment, exile : exsili poena: confugere in exsilium: civium, L.: civīs in exsilium eicio: in exilio aetatem agere, S.: esse in exsilio: quendam de exsilio reducere: revocare, L.: Ex…

exsisto.definition: ex-sistō or existō stitī, —, ere, to step out, come forth, emerge, appear: e latebris, L.: ab inferis: (bovis) a mediā fronte cornu exsistit, Cs.: nympha gurgite medio, O.: occultum malum exsistit, comes to light. — T…

exsolvo.definition: ex-solvō or exolvō solvī, solūtus, ere, to loose, unloose, set loose, release, deliver, free: te, T.: venas, to open, Ta.: toto paulatim se corpore, V. —Fig., to solve, resolve: nodum erroris, L.: obsidum, raise, Ta.:…

exsomnis.definition: exsomnis (exom-) e, adj. ex+somnus, sleepless, watchful : Vestibulum servat, V.: Euhias, H.

exsorbeo.definition: ex-sorbeō or exorbeō uī, —, ēre, to suck out, suck up, drain, drink: Pectora linguis, O.: civilem sanguinem.— Fig., to seize greedily: praedas. — To exhaust: viros, Iu. — To meet eagerly, welcome: difficultatem.

exspatior.definition: ex-spatior (expat-) ātus, ārī, dep., to wander from the way, spread, extend: exspatiantur equi, O.: Exspatiata flumina, i. e. overflowing, O.

exspectatio.definition: exspectātiō or expectātiō ōnis, f exspecto, an awaiting, expecting, expectation, longing, desire : caeca: praeter exspectationem, unexpectedly : magna: cum summā exspectatione populi R.: exspectationibus decipiendis: …

exspecto.definition: ex-spectō or expectō āvī, ātus, āre, to look out for, await, wait for : diem ex die, ut statuerem: alius alium exspectantes, S.: eventum pugnae, Cs.: ultima semper Exspectandi dies homini est, O.: cenantes comites, i.…

exspiratio.definition: exspīrātiō (expīr-) ō nis, f exspiro, a breathing out, exhalation : terrae.

exspiro.definition: ex-spīrō or expīrō āvī , ātus, āre, to breathe out, emit, blow out, exhale, give out: medios animam in ignīs, O.: flammas pectore, V.: Vis ventorum Exspirare aliquā cupiens, escape, O.—To breathe one's last, expire: e…

exsplendesco.definition: ex-splendēscō duī, ere, inch, to shine forth, be distinguished: clarius, N.

exspolio.definition: ex-spoliō āvī, ātus, āre, to spoil, pillage, plunder: urbem: hos vestro auxilio, Cs.: virtutem rerum selectione.

exspuo.definition: ex-spuō uī, ūtus, ere, to spit out, spit: vina, Iu.: hamum, O.—Fig., to expel, banish: miseriam ex animo, T.

exsterno.definition: exsternō āvī, ātus, āre 2 STAR-, to terrify greatly, affright : alqm luctibus, Ct.: (Io) se exsternata refugit, O.

exstillo.definition: ex-stīllō or extīllō ā vī, ātus, āre, to trickle away, melt: lacrumis si extillaveris, T.

exstimulator.definition: exstimulātor (ext-) ōris, m exstimulo, an inciter, instigator : rebellionis, Ta.: Verginii, Ta.

exstimulo.definition: ex-stimulō (ext-) āvī, ātus, āre, to goad on, instigate, stimulate: virum dictis, O.: Tigris Exstimulata fame, O.: fata cessantia, i. e. hasten death, O.

exstinctio.definition: exstinctiō ōnis, f STIG-, extinction, annihilation .

exstinctor.definition: exstinctor ōris, m STIG-, an extinguisher : incendi. — An annihilator, suppressor : patriae: latrocini.

exstinctus.definition: exstinctus (ext-) adj. P. of exstinguo, dead : Exstinctus amabitur, H.: Amphion, O.— Plur m . as subst: violare exstinctos, O.

exstinguo.definition: ex-stinguō or extinguō nxī (exstinxstī for exstinxistī, exstinxem for exstinxissem, V.), nctus, ere, to put out, quench, extinguish: lumina: ignis exstinguitur, goes out: ignem, V.— To deprive of life, kill, destroy: …

exstirpo.definition: ex-stirpō (ext-) āvī, ātus, āre, to root out, eradicate, extirpate: arbores, Cu. — Fig.: vitia: ex animo humanitatem.

exsto.definition: ex-stō or extō —, —, āre, to stand out, stand forth, project, protrude, extend above, tower: (milites) cum capite solo ex aquā exstarent, Cs.: super aequora celso collo, O.: summo pectore, Cs.: ferrum de pectore, O. —…

exstructio.definition: exstrūctiō or extrūctiō ō nis, f exstruo, a building up, erecting, structure : ea, quae, etc.— Plur: tectorum.

exstruo.definition: ex-struō or extruō ūxī, ūctus, ere, to pile, heap up, accumulate: materiam pro vallo, Cs.: acervum (librorum): exstructos disiecit montīs, V.: exstructis in altum divitiis, H.: tapetibus altis Exstructus, on a pile of…

exsudo.definition: ex-sūdō or exūdō āvī, ā tus, āre, to ooze, exude: exsudat inutilis umor, V. — To perform with sweating, toil through, undergo: causas, H.: certamen, L.

exsul.definition: exsul or exul ulis, m and f 2 SAL-, a banished person, wanderer, exile : capitis damnati exsulesque, Cs.: exsules restituti: pauper et exsul, homeless , H.: patriae quis exsul Se quoque fugit? H.: mundi, O.: nunc vero…

exsulo.definition: exsulō or exulō āvī, ātum, āre exsul, to be an exile, be banished, live in exile : Romae: in Volscos exsulatum abiit, L.: apud Prusiam: Protei ad usque columnas, V. — To be absent, be a stranger : domo, T.: animo.

exsultatio.definition: exsultātiō (exult-) ōnis, f exsulto, a leaping for joy, exultation , L.: Athamantis: par, Ta.

exsultim.definition: exsultim adv. 2 SAL-, leaping about, friskingly : ludit exsultim, H.

exsulto.definition: exsultō or exultō āvī, —, āre, freq. exsilio, to spring vigorously, leap up, jump up : equi ferocitate exsultantes: taurus in herbā, O.: in limine Pyrrhus, V.: exsultant aestu latices, V.: exsultantes undae, dancing ,…

exsuperabilis.definition: exsuperābilis (exup-) e, adj. exsupero, to be overcome : non exsuperabile saxum, V.

exsuperantia.definition: exsuperantia (exup-) ae, f exsupero, preeminence, superiority : virtutis.

exsupero.definition: ex-superō or exuperō āvī, ātus, āre, to mount up, tower: exsuperant flammae, V. — To surmount, pass over: iugum, V.: solum Helori, V. —Fig., to be superior, prevail, be conspicuous, excel: si non poterunt exsuperare, …

exsurdo.definition: exsurdō —, —, āre ex+surdus, to deafen, dull, blunt : palatum, H.

exsurgo.definition: ex-surgō or exurgō surrēxī, —, ere, to rise up, rise, get up, stand up: cum exsurgeret, simul, etc.: exsurge quaeso: ex insidiis, L.: temere, Ta.: altior, V.—Of the sun, Ta.: presso tellus aratro, Tb.: cum geminis exs…

exsuscito.definition: ex-suscitō (exusc-) āvī, ātus, āre, to rouse from sleep, awaken: te gallorum cantus exsuscitat.— To kindle: flammas aurā, O.: incendium, L. —Fig., to stir up, rouse up, excite: animos: animum dictis.

exta.definition: exta ōrum, n sup. for *ecista from ex, the chief internal organs of the body, significant organs (in prognostication): exta interpretari: dare, L.: inspicere: reddere Marti, V.: lustralia, V.: victimae, L.

extabesco.definition: ex-tābēscō buī, ere, inch, to pass away completely, disappear: corpus macie extabuit, Poët. ap. C.—Fig.: opiniones diuturnitate.

extemplo.definition: extemplō adv. ex+*tempulum, dim. of tempus, immediately, straightway, forthwith, without delay : quid fingat extemplo non habet: haec extemplo in invidiam, verterunt, L.: Dixit et extemplo sensit, etc., at once , V.: …

extemporalis.definition: extemporālis e, adj. ex+tempus, off hand, on the spur of the moment : audacia, Ta.

extendo.definition: ex-tendō tendī, tentus or tēnsus, ere, to stretch out, spread out, extend: extensis digitis: Buten harenā, stretch prostrate, V.: capita tignorum, Cs.: Maiores pennas nido, H.: aciem latius, Cu.: labellum, pout, Iu.: …

extenuatio.definition: extenuātiō ōnis, f extenuo, a lessening, diminution, extenuation (as a figure of speech).

extenuo.definition: ex-tenuō āvī, ātus, āre, to make small, reduce, diminish: aër extenuatus, rarefied: in aquas, O.: mediam aciem, L.: extenuatā acie, S. — Fig., to diminish, lessen, weaken, extenuate, detract from: laudes verbis: cuius…

exter.definition: (exter or exterus, tera, terum) adj. ex, on the outside, outward, of another country, foreign, strange . — Only plur: ius nationum exterarum: civitates: regna, V.; see also exterior, extimus, extremus.

exterebro.definition: (ex-terebrō) —, ātus, āre, to extract by boring, bore out: aurum.

extermino.definition: exterminō āvī, ātus, āre ex+terminus, to drive out, drive away, expel, exile, banish : Marcellum ex urbe: oppugnatores rei p. de civitate.—Fig., to drive out, put away, put aside, remove : auctoritatem vestram e civit…

externus.definition: externus adj. exter, outward, external : visio<*> vir rebus externis laudandus, foreign relations .—As subst m. : odium in externos, towards strangers .— As subst n. : externi ne quid, H.: illa externa, outward goods.…

extero.definition: ex-terō —, —, ere, to tread down, crush: nives, O.

exterreo.definition: ex-terreō uī, itus, ēre, to strike with terror, frighten, affright: praeter modum exterreri: urbem nuntius exterruit, Ta.: voltu legiones, Ta.: propriā exterrita voce est, i. e. lost her voice through fright, O.: Impr…

extimesco.definition: ex-timēscō muī, —, ere, inch, to be greatly afraid, fear greatly, await with fear, dread: equi repentinis sibilis extimescebant: de fortunis: ne id evenerit: Non extimui, quod, etc., V.: si filius venisset, posse exti…

extispex.definition: extispex icis, m exta + SPEC-, an observer of entrails, diviner, soothsayer .

extollo.definition: ex-tollō —, —, ere, to lift out, lift up, raise, elevate: iacentem: caput: pugionem, Ta.: in gremium liberorum ex te genus, Enn. ap. C.: gurgite palmas, Pr.—Fig., to raise, exalt: novos, S.: opibus et honoribus extoll…

extorqueo.definition: ex-torqueō sī, tus, ēre, to twist out, wrench out, wrest away: ferrum e manibus: horum gladios: dextrae mucronem, V.: in servilem modum extorti, wrenched, L.: extorque, put me to the torture, T.—To obtain by force, ex…

extorris.definition: extorris e, adj. ex + terra, driven out of the country, exiled, banished, homeless : hinc extorres profugerunt: agro Romano, L.: patriā domo, S.: extorre hinc Punicum nomen, driven from this land , L.: extorrem populu…

extortor.definition: extortor ōris, m TARC-, an extorter : Bonorum, T.

extraho.definition: ex-trahō āxī, āctus, ere, to draw out, draw forth, pull out, drag: telum e corpore: telum de volnere, O.: puerum alvo, H.: consulem ex tectis: rure in urbem, H.: senatores vi in publicum, L.: extractos ad certamen fud…

extraneus.definition: extrāneus adj. exter, from without, strange : nullum extraneum malum est: ornamenta.—As subst m., a stranger , L.— Plur., Ta.

extraordinarius.definition: extra-ōrdinārius adj., out of the common order, extraordinary, uncommon: pecuniae: reus, to be tried out of the usual order: cohortes, select, L.: porta (i. e. praetoria), L.: petitio consulatūs: imperium: periculum, Cu.

extrarius.definition: extrārius adj. extra, outward, external, extrinsic : res (opp. in corpore). — As subst m., a stranger , T.

extremitas.definition: extrēmitās ātis, f extremus, the extremity, end, terminus : mundi.—In geometry, the surface .

extremus.definition: extrēmus adj. sup. exter, outermost, utmost, extreme, farthest, last : oppidum Allobrogum, Cs.: finis provinciae, L.: Indi, H.: in codicis extremā cerā: extremā lineā amare, i. e. to make love at a distance , T.: vini…

extrico.definition: ex-trīcō āvī, ātus, āre ex + tricae, to disentangle, extricate, clear, free : extricata densis Cerva plagis, H.: nummos unde unde, procure with difficulty , H.—Fig., to unravel, clear up : nihil, Ph.

extrinsecus.definition: extrīnsecus adv. exter + secus, from without, from abroad : obiectā terribili re: spiritum adducere: imminens bellum, L.— Without, on the outside : inaurata (columna).

extrudo.definition: ex-trūdō sī, sus, ere, to thrust out, push forth, drive out, drive away: me foras, T.: Pollucem, get rid of: extrudi a senatu in Macedoniam: extruso mari aggere, shut out, Cs.: merces, to sell off, H.

extundo.definition: ex-tundō tudī, —, ere, to beat out, strike out, forge out: nobis hanc artem, devise, V.: ancilia, fashion in relief, V.: calcibus frontem, crush, Ph.: fastidia, drive off, H.

exturbo.definition: ex-turbō āvī, ātus, āre, to drive out, thrust out, drive away, thrust away: homines e possessionibus: alqm focis patriis: provinciā exturbatus: caede animas, O.: spem pacis, L.—To drive away (a wife), divorce: Octavia…

exubero.definition: ex-ūberō —, —, āre uber, to grow luxuriantly, be abundant, abound, overflow : luxuriā foliorum exuberat umbra, V.: alte spumis amnis, V.: pomis annus, V.: ex eruditione eloquentia, Ta.: animus fenore, revels , Ta.

exulcero.definition: ex-ulcerō āvī, ātus, āre, to make worse, exasperate, embitter: quae sanare nequeunt: exulceratus animus.

exululo.definition: ex-ululō —, ātus, āre, to howl, cry out, howl violently, O.—P. pass.: (Bacchis) exululata iugis, after howling, O.: mater, invoked with screams, O.

exundo.definition: ex-undō āvī, —, āre, to flow out, overflow: tura in litora exundant, are washed up, Ta.—Fig.: exundat eloquentia, Ta.

exuo.definition: exuō uī, ūtus, ere 4 AV-, to draw out, take off, pull off, put off : pharetram umero, O.: iugum, shake off , L.: caestū s, V.— To unclothe, divest, free, put forth : pellibus membra, H.: ossa lacertosque, bares , V.: …

exuro.definition: ex-ūrō ūssī, ūstus, ere, to burn out, burn up, consume: vivus exustus est: vicos: classem, V. —To dry up: loca exusta solis ardoribus, S.: paludem, V.—To consume, destroy: aliis scelus exuritur igni, V.: cornua, O.: e…

exustio.definition: exūstiō ōnis, f exustus, a burning up, conflagration : exustiones terrarum.

exuviae.definition: exuviae ārum, f 4 AV-, that which is stripped off, clothing, equipments, arms : pyram Erige exuviasque omnīs super imponant, V.: (coluber) positis novus exuviis, his slough , V.: leonis, skin , V.: ferarum, O.: devota…

excellens.definition: excellēns entis, adj. with comp. and sup. P. of excello, towering, prominent, distinguished, superior, surpassing, excellent : animus ac virtus: vir virtute: inter tot unus: studium, Cs.: cycnus, of surpassing beauty …

elegans.definition: ēlegāns antis, adj. with comp. and sup. for ēligēns, P. of eligo, accustomed to select, fastidious, nice, delicate : heia, ut elegans est! T.: qui se elegantīs dici volunt: elegantissimus poëta, N. — Select, choice, n…

explanate.definition: (explānātē) adv. explanatus, plainly, clearly, distinctly .—Only comp: definire rem.

evocatus.definition: ēvocātus adj. P. of evoco, called out.— Plur. m . as subst, reënlisted veterans , Cs., S.

efferatus.definition: efferātus (ecf-) adj. with comp. P. of 2 effero, wild, savage, fierce : multa: mores efferatiores, L.

extra.definition: extrā adv. and praep. exter. I. Adv. (for comp. see exterius), on the outside, without : extra et intus hostem habere, Cs.: et in corpore et extra: illa, quae sunt extra, outward goods .—In the phrase, extra quam: ext…

excors.definition: excors cordis, adj. ex + cor, without intelligence, without understanding, senseless, silly, stupid : anus: hoc qui non videt, excors est: admodum: turpis et excors, H.

eiulo.definition: ēiulō —, —, āre 2 ei, to wail, lament .

effugium.definition: effugium ī, n ex + 2 FVG-, a fleeing, flight, escape, avoidance, way of escape, means of flight : mortis: pennarum, by means of : naves peritis nandi dedissent effugium, L.: ad effugium navem habere, L.: in publicum, …

extumefactus.definition: extumefactus adj. ex-tumeo + facio, swollen : (pars animi) potu (B. & K.).

expetendus.definition: expetendus adj. P. of expeto, worth striving for, desirable : gloria.

Euhias.definition: Euhiās or Euiās adis, f , eu)ia/s, a Bacchante, H.

enucleatus.definition: ēnucleātus adj. P. of enucleo, pure, clean : suffragia, free from undue influence : genus dicendi, unadorned .

explorate.definition: explōrātē adv. with comp. exploratus, for a certainty, securely, surely : haec scribo: exploratius promittere.

enimvero.definition: enim-vērō or enim vērō adv., yes indeed, yes truly, assuredly, of a truth, to be sure, indeed: Enimvero Chremes cruciat adulescentulum, T.: enim vero ferendum hoc quidem non est: hic enim vero tu exclamas, etc.: tum e…

exolesco.definition: ex-olēscō olēvī, ētus, ere, inch, to grow out of use, become obsolete, pass away, cease: cum patris favor exolevisset, L.: exoletis annalium exemplis, L.: exolescunt Graeci amictūs, Ta.: ne disciplina per desidiam exo…

ecquando.definition: ec-quandō adv. interrog, ever, at any time: ecquando te rationem redditurum putasti?: quotiens hoc agitur, ecquandone nisi? etc.: quaero ecquando creati sint, etc., whether ever.

exlex.definition: ex-lēx ēgis, adj., beyond the law, bound by no law, lawless: exlegem esse Sullam putare: spectator, H.

expolitus.definition: expolītus adj. with comp. P. of expolio, polished, smooth : expolitior dens, Ct.— Refined : vir vitā.

extremo.definition: extrēmō adv. extremus, at last, finally Hamilcarem imperatorem fecerunt, N.

eculeus.definition: eculeus (equu-) ī, m dim. equus, a young horse, foal, colt : in equo quam in eculeo.— A small equestrian statue : eculeos argenteos aufert. — A rack, torture-horse : facti in eculeo quaestio est.

eventura.definition: ēventūra ōrum, n P. n. of evenio, that which will happen : eventura precor, i. e. my prayers shall be fulfilled , Tb.

eiero.definition: ēierō or ēiūrō āvī , ātus, āre ex + IV-, to refuse upon oath, reject by oath, abjure : id forum sibi iniquum eierare, make oath that the tribunal is prejudiced : me iniquum: bonam copiam, i. e. make oath of insolvency…

ecquinam.definition: ecquīnam quaenam, quodnam (no gen. or dat.), pron interrog. adj. ecqui + nam.—Direct, Is there any? any? ecquodnam principium putatis? etc. —Indirect, whether any, if any : dubium, ecquaenam fieri possit accessio.

excelse.definition: (excelsē) adv. excelsus, in an elevated tone, loftily .— Only comp: excelsius dicere.

evalidus.definition: ē-validus adj., very strong, mighty: spina.

excitus.definition: excitus and excītus P. of excieo and excio.

enixe.definition: ēnīxē adv. with comp. enixus, strenuously, earnestly, zealously : causam suscipere: Caesarem iuvabat, Cs.: enixius ad bellum adiuvare, L.

extenuatus.definition: extenuātus adj. with sup. P. of extenuo, trifling, faint, weak : vestigia, Ct.: oratio, Her.: (copiolae) extenuatissimae, Brut. ad C.

emptum.definition: ēmptum ī, n emptus, a purchase, contract of purchase : quae ex empto aut vendito contra fidem fiunt, in buying and selling .

eiaculor.definition: ē-iaculor ātus, ārī, dep., to shoot out, throw out: aquas, O.: se in altum, O.

effutuo.definition: effutuō (ecf-) —, ūtus, ere ex + futuo, to exhaust by indulgence : ecfututa latera, Ct.

exspectatus.definition: exspectātus adj. with sup. P. of exspecto, anxiously expected, longed for, desired, welcome : carus omnibus exspectatusque venies: seges, V.: exspectati ad amplissimam dignitatem fratres, i. e. thought worthy of the h…

eiulatus.definition: ēiulātus plur nom., ūs, m eiulo, a wailing, loud lamentation : Philoctetae.

effrenatus.definition: effrēnātus adj. with comp. ex + frenatus, unbridled, without a rein : equi, L.—Fig., ungoverned, unrestrained, unbridled : homines secundis rebus: libido effrenatior, L.: cupiditas: effrenatior vox: ecfrenati libidine.

exsors.definition: ex-sors or exors sortis, adj., without lot, not assigned by lot: te voluit exsortem ducere honores (i. e. praeter ordinem), V. (al. honorem).— Having no share in, free from, deprived of: dulcis vitae, V.: amicitiae, L…

expetens.definition: expetēns entis, adj. P. of expeto, desirous, eager : in voluptatibus.

eclogarii.definition: eclogāriī ōrum, m ecloga, select passages .

exquisitus.definition: exquīsītus adj. with comp. and sup. P. of exquiro, carefully sought out, ripely considered, choice, excellent, exquisite : sententia: iudicium litterarum: munditia nimis: exquisitius dicendi genus: laudari exquisitiss…

exterior.definition: exterior us, adj. comp. exter, outward, outer, exterior : vallus, Cs.: contra exteriorem hostem, Cs.: comes exterior, i. e. on the left side , H.

emendatus.definition: ēmendātus adj. P. of emendo, correct, faultless, perfect : mores: vir, H.: locutio: carmina, H.: emendata maxime.

extimus.definition: extimus or extumus adj. sup. ex, outermost, farthest, most remote : orbis. — Plur n . as subst: umor Extuma possedit, O.

editum.definition: (ēditum ī), n editus.—Only plur. — Heights, elevations : montium, Ta., Cu.— Commands, orders : Thaumantidos, O.

eiectamentum.definition: ēiectāmentum ī, n eiecto, refuse, jetsam.— Plur. : cetera maris, Ta.

ecquid.definition: ecquid adv. interrog. neut. of ecquis.—Direct, at all? ecquid te pudet? T.: ecquid vides, quos, etc.: ecquid sentitis? etc., L.: Ecquid animos excitat Hector? V.—Indirect, whether, if at all : petisse, ecquid hanc rem…

elucubror.definition: ēlūcubror ātus, ārī, dep. elucubro, to work out at night, toil over : epistulam.

efferitas.definition: efferitās (ecf-) ātis, f efferus, wildness, barbarism : omnem ecferitatem expuli.

excelsus.definition: excelsus adj. with comp. and sup. P. of excello, elevated, lofty, high : locus, T.: mons, Cs.: vertex montis, V.: signum: in excelsiore loco: cornu excelsius, Cs.: mons excelsissimus, Cs.—As subst n., a height : simul…

effectum.definition: effectum ī, n P. n. of efficio, an effect .

elutus.definition: (ēlūtus) adj. P. of eluo, washed out, watery . — Only comp: inriguo nihil est elutius horto, H.

elatus.definition: ēlātus adj. P. of effero, exalted, lofty, high : animus: verba, high-sounding : animis superbis, V.: insula opibus, N.

exercitatus.definition: exercitātus adj. with comp. and sup. exercito; freq. of exerceo, well exercised, practised, versed, trained, experienced, disciplined : ad hanc rem, T.: in re militari: superioribus proeliis, Cs.: exercitatiores ad be…

expedite.definition: expedītē adv. with comp. and sup. expeditus, without impediment, without difficulty, readily, promptly, quickly : explicans quod proposuerat: expeditius navigans: te expeditissime conferas.

effuse.definition: effūsē adv. with comp. effusus, far spread, in disorder, at random : ire, S.: fugientes, L.: sequi, L.: effusius praedari, L. — Fig., profusely, lavishly, extravagantly : donare: vivere: animus exsultat: hospitiis eff…

equiria.definition: equīria ōrum, n equus, annual races in the Campus Martius, in honor of Mars , O.

escaria.definition: ēscāria ōrum, n esca, dishes, plate , Iu.

explanatus.definition: explānātus adj. P. of explano, plain, distinct : vocum impressio, i. e. ability to articulate .

excussus.definition: excussus adj. P. of excutio, stretched out, stiff : lacertus, O.

excellentia.definition: excellentia ae, f excellens, superiority, excellence : animi.—Plur: (in amicitiā).

egregie.definition: ēgregiē adv. with comp. egregius, excellently, eminently, surpassingly, splendidly, exceedingly, singularly : studere, T.: fecerat hoc: vincere, brilliantly , L.: Dixeris, H.: cordatus, Enn. ap. C.: factus: munitum op…

ellum.definition: ellum for en illum; see en.

exadversus.definition: ex-adversus (-vorsus) adv. and praep, over against, opposite.—As adv.: pistrilla, et exadvorsum fabrica, T.: exadvorsum ei loco Tonstrina erat, T.—As praep. with acc: exadversus eum locum: exadversum Athenas, N.

expositus.definition: expositus adj. P. of expono, open, accessible : Sunion, O.: Zephyris Lilybaeon, O. — Fig., common, vulgar : nihil expositum deducere, Iu.

erratum.definition: errātum ī, n 1 erro, an error, mistake, fault : commune: nullum ob erratum: minimum: errata officiis superes, S.: errata aetatis meae.

exstructum.definition: exstrūctum ī, n exstructus, a lofty seat : exstructoque resedit, V.

exsuctus.definition: exsūctus P. ex-sugo, drawn out, extracted, dried : medulla, H.: Ossa exsucta medullis, Iu.

electrum.definition: ēlectrum ī, n , h)/lektron, electrum, an alloy of gold and silver: liquidum, V.: attonitus pro Electro, his plate, Iu.—Amber, a fossil gum from the Baltic sea, O.—Plur: Pinguia, V.

eccam.definition: eccam i. e. ecce eam; see ecce.

exin.definition: exin or (old and late) exim for exinde, adv. —In place, thence, after that, next in order, next : (mare) ... exin aër: exim ventum Elephantinen, Ta.— After that, thereafter, then : Exin compellare pater me voce videtu…

escensus.definition: (ēscēnsus, ūs) m ex + SCAND-, a scaling . — Only abl sing. : capta escensu munimenta, by storm , Ta.

ebulum.definition: ebulum ī, n AMBR-, Dane-wort, dwarf-elder , V.

exorsa.definition: exōrsa ōrum, n 1 exorsus, a beginning, commencement : longa, preamble , V.: sua cuique exorsa laborem ferent, V.

extortus.definition: extortus adj. P. of extorqueo, deformed , puella, Iu.

epitaphios.definition: epitaphios ī, m , e)pita/fios, a funeral oration.

effusus.definition: effūsus adj. with comp. and sup, poured out, extensive, vast, broad, wide: late mare, H.: loca, Ta.: incendium, L.—Relaxed, slackened, loosened, dishevelled: quam potuit effusissimis habenis, L.: comae, O.: (nymphae) …

ecquo.definition: ecquō adv. interrog. ecqui, to any point? to any result? ecquo te provehere?

egens.definition: egēns entis, adj. with comp. and sup. P. of egeo, needy, necessitous, in want, poor : egens relictast misera, T.: egentes abundant: delectus egentium, Cs.: nil magnae laudis, not craving , V.: non rationis, not destit…

exspersus.definition: exspersus P. ex-sparsus, sprinkled, splashed : sanieque exspersa natarent Limina, V.

explicitus.definition: (explicitus) adj. P. of explico, unobstructed, practicable .—Only comp: (consilium), Cs.

eugae.definition: eugae (euge) interj., eu)=ge, bravo! well done! good! hurrah!: eugae habeo optumam, T. — Ironic.: eugae, iam lepidus vocor, excellent! T.

efficaciter.definition: (efficāciter) adv. efficax, efficaciously, effectually .—Only comp: efficacius agere, L.: obligari, Ta.

efflagitatus.definition: (efflāgitātus, ūs) m efflagito, an urgent solicitation .—Only abl sing. : meo.

exundans.definition: exundāns ntis, adj. P. of exundo, overflowing, abundant : ingenii fons, Iu.

eiecto.definition: ēiectō āvī, ātus, āre, freq. eicio, to cast out, throw up : harenas, O.: cruorem Ore, V.

enervatus.definition: ēnervātus adj. P. of enervo, unnerved, weakly, effeminate, unmanly : homines: ratio et oratio: sententia.

effatum.definition: effātum (ecf-) ī, n effatus, an utterance, axiom .

expensum.definition: expēnsum ī P. n. of expensus, money paid, a payment : codex accepti et expensi, receipts and disbursements : tabulae accepti et expensi.

exedrium.definition: exedrium (exhe-) ī, n , e)ce/drion, a sittingroom, parlor: exedria nova in porticulā.

exoptatus.definition: exoptātus adj. with comp. and sup. P. of exopto, greatly wished, earnestly desired, longed for : nuntius: parens, V.: nihil exoptatius adventu meo: exoptatissima gratulatio.

evolsio.definition: ēvolsiō (ēvul-) ōnis, f ex + 2 VEL-, a pulling out : dentis.

eadem.definition: eādem adv. abl f. of īdem; sc. viā , by the same way : ventum est, eādem quā, etc.: revertens, L.: escendens descendensque, S. — At the same time, likewise , T.

exiliter.definition: exīliter adv., thinly, meagrely: verba exanimata: annales scripti: ad calculos revocare amicitiam, illiberally.

excitatus.definition: excitātus adj. with comp. P. of excito, lively, vehement, excited : sonus: clamor excitatior, L.: fortuna, rising .

expeditus.definition: expedītus adj. with comp. and sup. P. of expedio, unfettered, unimpeded, unencumbered, without a burden : in Galliam proficisci: Sagana, tucked up , H.: legiones, without baggage , Cs.: expedito exercitu pervenit, Ta.…

excessus.definition: excessus ūs, m 1 CAD-, a departure, demise : e vitā : Romuli.— A digression , Ta.

extremum.definition: extrēmum adv. extremus, at last, finally , C.: liquefacta Tabuit, O.— For the last time : te adfari, V.: Adloquor amicos, O.

exheres.definition: ex-hērēs ēdis, adj., disinherited: paternorum bonorum filius.

enodate.definition: ēnōdātē adv. with comp. enodatus, lucidly, explicitly : narrare: enodatius explicare.

effeminatus.definition: effēminātus adj. with sup. P. of effemino, womanish, effeminate : ne quid effeminatum sit: languor effeminatissimus: vox stupris effeminata.

edendum.definition: edendum ī, n P. of 1 edo, victuals, food : penuria edendi, V.

emendate.definition: ēmendātē adv. emendatus, faultlessly, perfectly : loqui.

exsecratus.definition: exsecrātus (execr-) adj. P. of exsecror, accursed, execrable, detestable : populo R.: columna.

expertus.definition: expertus adj. P. of experior, tried, proved, known by experience : vir expertae virtutis, L.: libertatis dulcedine nondum expertā, L.: miles, Ta.: per omnia, L.— Experienced in : belli iuvenes, V.

ecquisnam.definition: ecquisnam quidnam (no gen. or dat.), pron interrog. subst. ecquis + nam.—Direct, any one? anybody? Ecquisnam tibi dixerit, etc. — Indirect, whether any one : interrogare, ecquosnam posset nominare.

enuntiatum.definition: ēnūntiātum ī, n P. of enuntio, a proposition .

elegeia.definition: elegēia ae, f , e)legei/a, an elegy, elegiac song: elegeia cantet Amores, O.

excieo.definition: ex-cieō and ex-ciō īvī, ītus and itus, ī re, rarely ēre (imperf. excībat, L.), to call out, summon forth, rouse: consulem ab urbe, L.: animas sepulcris, V.: artifices e Graeciā, Cu.: Antiochum in Graeciam, L.: Volscos…

expletus.definition: explētus adj. P. of expleo, full, complete, perfect : rerum comprehensio: undique forma honestatis.

emeritus.definition: ē-meritus adj., that has finished work, past service: equi, O.: aratrum, O.: acus, Iu.—Plur m. as subst, discharged veterans, Ta.

eventum.definition: ēventum ī, n P. n. of evenio, an occurrence, chance, event : causae eventorum.— That which befalls, experience, fortune : te ex nostris eventis communibus admonendum: pendere ex alterius eventis.— An issue, consequenc…

effrenate.definition: effrēnātē adv. with comp. effrenatus, unrestrainedly, violently : incitari: effrenatius in aciem inrupere.

exigue.definition: exiguē adv. exiguus, shortly, slightly, scantily, sparingly, exactingly, barely, meagrely : nimis exigue ad calculos revocare amicitiam: Praebent sumptum, T.: frumentum exigue dierum XXX habere, Cs.: epistula scripta.

erectus.definition: ērēctus adj. with comp. P. of erigo, set up, upright, elevated, lofty : (homines) erectos constituit: voltus, O.: prorae, Cs.—Fig., elevated, lofty, noble : celsus et erectus: ingenium, Ta.: si quis est paulo erectior…

exspes.definition: ex-spēs adj. (only nom sing.), without hope, hopeless: inops, exspes, O.: enatat exspes, H.

efficiens.definition: efficiēns entis, adj. P. of efficio, effective, efficient, producing, active : res: virtus efficiens utilitatis, the producer : ea, quae sunt efficientia voluptatum.

expressus.definition: expressus adj. with comp. P. of exprimo, clearly exhibited, distinct, manifest, clear, plain, express : species deorum, quae nihil habeat expressi: litterae lituraeque. — Fig., distinct, real : signa virtutum: sceleri…

extentus.definition: extentus adj. with sup. P. of extendo, extended, extensive, wide : latius Lucrino Stagna lacu, H.: extentissima vallis, L.

eiulatio.definition: ēiulātiō ōnis, f eiulo, a wailing, lamenting : lugubris: non virilis, H.

edictum.definition: ēdictum ï, n edico, a proclamation, ordinance, edict, manifesto (of a magistrate or generalin-chief): consul praetor nova edicta proponunt: civem edicto eicere: proconsulis, L.: rex Edicto vetuit ne quis, etc., H. — E…

epodes.definition: epodes um, m a kind of sea-fish, O.

escunt.definition: escunt old for erunt; see sum.

eiectio.definition: ēiectiō ōnis, f eicio, a casting out, banishment, exile .

eminens.definition: ēminēns entis, adj. with comp. P. of emineo, standing out, projecting, prominent, high, lofty : oculi: promunturia, Cs.: saxa, S.: genae leniter: trabes eminentiores, Cs.: per inaequaliter eminentia rupis, irregular s…

exsultans.definition: exsultāns (exult-) ntis, adj. P. of exsulto, boastful, vainglorious : animus, Ta.: supra modum, Ta.

exterius.definition: exterius adv. exterior, on the outer side, without : sitae (urbes), O.

extergeo.definition: (ex-tergeō) —, sus, ēre, to strip clean, plunder: fanum extersum relinquere.

eruditus.definition: ērudītus adj. with comp. and sup. P. of erudio, instructed, educated, learned, accomplished , informed, skilled, experienced : quas (artī s) qui tenent eruditi appellantur: Graeculus: rebus gestis: litteris eruditior …

effertus.definition: effertus adj. P. of effarcio, crammed, rich : arva Asiae, poet. ap. C.

ellam.definition: ellam for en illam; see en.

exploratus.definition: explōrātus adj. with comp. and sup. P. of exploro, ascertained, established, settled, certain, sure, safe : Iam id exploratumst, T.: consulatus: victoria, Cs.: litterae exploratae a timore, i. e. affording certainty :…

ecfatus.definition: ecfātus, ecferō, ecfor, ecfutuō etc., see eff-.

erratus.definition: (errātus, ūs) m 1 erro, a wandering, winding .— Only abl plur. : longis erratibus actus, O.

eodem.definition: eōdem adv. of place old dat. and locat. of idem. I. Locat. use; with loci, in the same place : res eodem est loci quo reliquisti.— II. Dat. uses, to the same place, to the same point, thither : clientes suos eodem con…

Echidneus.definition: Echidnēus adj., of Echidna (a monster, mother of Cerberus): canis, Cerberus, O.

erudite.definition: (ērudītē) adv. eruditus, learnedly, with erudition .—Only comp. and sup: eruditius disputare: litterae eruditissime scriptae.

exactus.definition: exāctus adj. with comp. P. of exigo, precise, accurate, exact : numerus, L.: fides, O.: morum exactior, O.—Plur n . as subst: sociis exacta referre, V.

endoploratus.definition: endoplōrātus P. endoploro, old for imploro, to cry for help : endoplorato, ut, etc., a cry for help having been raised , C. (old form.).

enucleo.definition: ēnucleō —, —, āre ex + nucleus. — Fig., to lay open, explain in detail : haec nunc: argumenta.

eversus.definition: ēversus. 1. P. of everro.— 2. P. of everto.

exsiccatus.definition: exsiccātus adj. P. of exsicco, dried up, dry, jejune : orationis genus.

e.definition: ē: forma di ex davanti a consonante — + abl.: da, fuori da

epos.definition: epos (only acc.), n , e)/pos, a heroic poem, H.

elaboratus.definition: ēlabōrātus adj. P. of elaboro, highly wrought, finished, labored : versūs: concinnitas: non elaboratus pes, i. e. a simple strain , H.: alqs in verbis, Ta.

etesiae.definition: etēsiae ārum, m , e)thsi/ai, Etesian winds, trade-winds, N. W. winds which prevail in summer in the eastern parts of the Mediterranean Sea: venti: etesiis tenebatur, Cs.

evolgo.definition: ē-volgō (-vulgō) āvī, ātus, āre, to make commonly known, divulge: civile ius, L.: sic evulgari iussit, laurum additum (esse), etc., Ta.: evolgatus pudor, i. e. public exposure, Ta.

excusate.definition: (excūsātē) adv. excuso, without blame .— Only comp: excusatius excipere, Ta.

evidenter.definition: ēvidenter adv. evidens, evidently, manifestly, obviously : paenitere, L.

enixus.definition: ēnīxus adj. P. of enitor, strenuous, earnest, zealous : studium, L.: virtus, L.

eburneus.definition: eburneus adj. ebur, of ivory : dentes, elephants' tusks : signum: colla, white as ivory , O.

exquisite.definition: exquīsītē adv. with comp. exquisitus, carefully, accurately, particularly, excellently : de eo crimine disputare: quae (rationes) exquisitius conliguntur.

epiredia.definition: epirēdia ōrum, n e)pi/ + raeda, traces , Iu (acc. to others, carts, wagons ).

eximie.definition: eximiē adv. eximius, exceedingly, very much, uncommonly, excellently : Plotium dilexit: cenare, Iu.: polliceri omnia, L.

exanimis.definition: exanimis e, adj. ex + anima, lifeless, dead : (columba) Decidit exanimis, V.: ut exanimem labentem ex equo Scipionem vidit, L.: artūs, O.— Fig., breathless, terrified, dismayed : legiones vice unius, with suspense for…

eiusdem.definition: ēiusdem modī, ēius modī see modus.

eluvies.definition: ēluviēs —, em, ē, f ex + 3 LV-, an overflow, inundation : eluvie mons est deductus in aequor, O.: maris, Ta.: eluvies iter morabantur, Cu.— A washing away, discharge : conducere Siccandam eluviem, removal of sewage , …

ensiger.definition: ēnsiger gera, gerum, adj. ensis + GES-, sword-bearing : Orion, O.

enubo.definition: ē-nūbō nūpsī, —, ere, to marry away, marry (to a stranger), L.—To marry out of one's rank: filias e patribus, L.

euhans.definition: euhāns or euāns antis P. (the cry of the Bacchantes), crying euhan! Ct., Pr.—Poet. with acc: euhantīs orgia Ducebat Phrygias, celebrating the rites of Bacchus with the cry euhan! V.

exuvium.definition: exuvium ī, n 4 AV-, spoils, booty : exuvio plenus ab hoste redis, Pr.

evagor.definition: ē-vagor ātus, ārī, dep., to wander forth, march to and fro, manœuvre: effuse, L.: ad evagandum spatium, for evolutions, L. — Fig., to spread, extend: qui appetitū s longius evagantur: late vis morbi, L. — With acc: or…

expromptus.definition: exprōmptus adj. P. of expromo, ready, at hand : malitia atque astutia, T.

exardesco.definition: ex-ārdēscō ārsī, ārsus, ere, inch, to blaze out, kindle, take fire: materies facilis ad exardescendum.— Fig., to be kindled, be inflamed, break out, be exasperated, be provoked, rage: iracundiā ac stomacho: dolore, Cs…

endo.definition: endo praep. old form of in, in : endo caelo, C. (XII Tabb.).

Eleleides.definition: Elelēides —, f Eleleus, the Bacchae , O.

experiens.definition: experiēns entis, adj. with sup. P. of experior, experienced, enterprising, active, industrious : homo: vir, L.: experientissimus arator: genus experiens laborum, used to , O.

existimantes.definition: (exīstimantēs) ium, m P. plur. of existimo, critics, critical judges .

evago.definition: ē-vagor ātus, ārī, dep., to wander forth, march to and fro, manœuvre: effuse, L.: ad evagandum spatium, for evolutions, L. — Fig., to spread, extend: qui appetitū s longius evagantur: late vis morbi, L. — With acc: or…

expulso.definition: expulsor ōris, m 1 PAL-, a driver out, expeller : bonorum: tyranni, N.

exfervo.definition: ef-fervō —, —, ere, to boil up, boil over: in agros Aetnam, V.: apes ruptis costis (boum), swarm out, V.

excaedo.definition: 1) excidō cidī, —, ere ex + cado, to fall out, drop down, fall away : sol excidisse mihi e mundo videtur: dentīs Excidere videre, H.: mihi Excidit cera, from my hand , O.: Palinurus Exciderat puppi, V.: in flumen (sc. e … | 2) excīdō īdī, īsus, ere ex + caedo, to cut out, cut off, hew out, cut down : arbores, Cs.: excisa arbor: columnas rupibus, V.— To raze, demolish, lay waste, destroy : aedīs: Troiam, V.: Sugambros, Ta.—Fig., to drive out…

exquaero.definition: exquīrō sīvī, sītus, ere ex+quaero, to search out, seek diligently, inquire into, scrutinize, inquire, ask : ex te causas divinationis: haec nimis a Graecis, to be too exacting in : Ancillas cruciatu, T.: secum, quid …

excurso.definition: excursor ōris, m 1 CEL-, a skirmisher, scout, spy : istius.

exceptor.definition: exceptō āvī, ātus, āre, freq. excipio, to take out, take up, catch : barbatulos de piscinā: hos (milites), Cs.: auras, to snuff up , V.

excusor.definition: excūsō āvī, ātus, āre ex +*causo; 1 CAV- —With pers. obj., to excuse, make an excuse for : Atticae me: se de consilio, Cs.: me apud Apuleium: ut excuser morbi causā: si iudex excusetur Areopagites esse, pleads as his …

edo.definition: 1) edō ēdī, ēsus, ere, or ēsse (ē st for edit; ēsses, ēsset, for ederes, etc., V., H., O., Iu.; ēstur, O.—Subj: edit for edat, H.; edint, C.) ED-, to eat, consume : de symbolis, T.: ut biberent, quoniam esse nollent: ut … | 2) ē-dō didī, ditus, ere, to give out, put forth, bring forth, raise, set up: animam, i. e. die: vitam, to end: spiritum: clamorem, utter: voces: questūs, O.: Maeander in sinum maris editur, discharges, L.: ordo editus i…

educo.definition: 1) ē - dūcō dūxī, ductus, ere, to lead forth, draw out, bring off, take away: eos nobiscum: (medicum) tecum, i. e. to your province: impedimenta ex castris educi iussit, carried, Cs.: gladium, draw, Cs.: gladiis eductis:… | 2) ēducō āvī, ātus, āre DVC-, to bring up, rear, train, educate : unā a pueris educti, T.: apud alquem: illum primis cunis, O.: ars dicendi ea educat, develops : educata huius nutrimentis eloquentia.— To produce, support…

effectus.definition: 1) 'effectus P. of efficio.' | 2) effectus ūs, m ex + 2 FAC-, an effecting, execution, accomplishment, performance : peccare sine effectu, i. e. an outward act : operis, L.: opera in effectu erant, nearly done , L.: spei, L.— An operation, effect, res…

effero.definition: 1) efferō or ecferō extulī, ēlātus, ferre ex + fero, to carry out, take out, bring forth, take away, remove : tela ex aedibus: extra aedīs puerum, T.: frumentum ab Ilerdā, Cs.: signa portis efferri vidit, L.: pedem, esca… | 2) efferō āvī, ātus, āre efferus, to make wild, make savage, barbarize, brutalize : terram immanitate beluarum efferari: speciem oris, L.: gentes inmanitate efferatae: efferari militiā animos, L.: Thebanos ad odium Roman…

egressus.definition: 1) ēgressus P. of egredior. | 2) ēgressus ūs, m egredior, a going out, going away, egress, departure : vestrum egressum ornando: arcet egressu (ventos), O.: egressūs eius explorat, tracks his movements , S.— A disembarking, landing : optimum esse egr…

eo.definition: 1) eō īvī or iī (3d pers. rarely ī t, V.; inf. īvisse or. īsse), itūrus (P. praes. iēns, euntis; ger. eundum), īre 1 I-, to go, walk, ride, sail, fly, move, pass : In in malam rem, T.: subsidio suis ierunt, Cs.: quocumqu… | 2) eō adv. old dat. and abl. of pron. stem I-. I. Locat. and abl. uses, there, in that place : cum tu eo quinque legiones haberes.—Fig.: res erat eo iam loci, ut, etc., in such a condition.—Therefore, on that account, fo…

erro.definition: 1) errō āvī, ātus, āre, to wander, stray, rove, roam: cum vagus et exsul erraret: non certis passibus, O.: circum villulas nostras: per urbem, L.—Pass impers.: solis erratur in agris, V.—Of things: quae (stellae) errante… | 2) errō ōnis, m 1 erro, a wanderer, vagabond : fugitivus erro, H.— A wanderer in love , Tb.

evito.definition: 1) ē-vītō āvī, ātus, āre, to shun, avoid: meta Evitata rotis, H.: fraxinum, O.: causas suspicionum: tela amictu, Ct. | 2) ēvītō āvī, —, āre ex + vita, to deprive of life, kill : Priamo vi vitam evitari, Enn. ap. C.

examen.definition: 1) exāmen inis, n ex + 1 AG-, a multitude flying out, swarm : apium: vesparum, L.: cum prima sui ducent examina reges, V.— A multitude, crowd, shoal, swarm : examinibus suis agros operire, L.: iuvenum, H.: servorum. | 2) exāmen inis, n ex + 2 AG-, the tongue of a balance : aequato examine lances Sustinet, V.—Fig., a weighing, consideration : legum, O.

excido.definition: 1) excidō cidī, —, ere ex + cado, to fall out, drop down, fall away : sol excidisse mihi e mundo videtur: dentīs Excidere videre, H.: mihi Excidit cera, from my hand , O.: Palinurus Exciderat puppi, V.: in flumen (sc. e … | 2) excīdō īdī, īsus, ere ex + caedo, to cut out, cut off, hew out, cut down : arbores, Cs.: excisa arbor: columnas rupibus, V.— To raze, demolish, lay waste, destroy : aedīs: Troiam, V.: Sugambros, Ta.—Fig., to drive out…

excursus.definition: 1) 'excursus P. of excurro.' | 2) excursus ūs, m 1 CEL-, a running out, running forth, excursion : excursūsque brevīs temptant (apes), V.— A sally, charge, inroad, invasion : militum, Cs.: subiti, Ta.

exercitus.definition: 1) exercitus adj. P. of exerceo, disciplined , experienced, versed : miles: ad omne flagitium, Ta.: consuetudine velare odium, Ta.: militiā, Ta.: eloquentia, of a practised speaker , Ta. — Vexed, harassed : omnibus iniqu… | 2) exercitus ūs (dat. ū, Cs., L.; gen plur. tūm, L.) exerceo, a disciplined body of men, army : terrestris, L.: tiro, L.: pedester, N.: exercitum dimittere, T.: comparare: parare, S.: scribere, L.: contrahere, Cs.: ducer…

exitus.definition: 1) 'exitus P. of exeo.' | 2) exitus ūs, m ex + 1 I-, a going out, going forth, egress, departure : omni exitu interclusi, Cs.: hominum exitū s adservare, Cs.: ne exitus inclusis ab urbe esset, L.— A way of egress, outlet, passage : angustus porta…

exortus.definition: 1) 'exortus P. of exorior.' | 2) exortus ūs, m 1 OL-, a coming forth, rising : solis exortūs, L.: lucis, Cu.

explicatus.definition: 1) explicātus adj. with comp. P. of explico, spread out : planissimo in loco.— Well ordered : causa: provincia.— Plain, clear : solutio: quibus (litteris) nihil explicatius.— Assured, certain : ratio salutis suae. | 2) explicātus ūs, m explico, an unfolding, exposition : difficilīs explicatūs habere.

excio.definition: exciō, -īre, -īvī, -ītum (anche excieō): far uscire, chiamar fuori, destare, suscitare

exardeo.definition: exārdeō, -ēre (cfr. exardescō, -ere, -ārsī): ardere, infiammarsi (d'ira, di passione)

expecto.definition: expectō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum (grafia di exspectō): aspettare, attendere; sperare

evangelizo.definition: ēvangelizō, -āre [crist.]: evangelizzare, annunciare il vangelo (gr. εὐαγγελίζομαι)
